local_repairs_on_final_route.issue: other (self-detected overreach: first moment vs path law)

lesson.obstruction: Sec 2 (L70-72) had said that exposing the cycles missing P leaves a hole process conditioned on every remaining cycle hitting P, and that the exterior calculation identifies 'its' next-pin first moment. Re-examination shows the exterior identity holds BEFORE the conditioning on G_{A0}; after conditioning, the determinant/Schur-complement calculation identifies only the conditional MEAN next-pin kernel, not the law of the conditioned paths. The comparison walk refreshes its complementary randomness on each circuit and does not repeat the actual loop trajectory.

lesson.generality: local (but load-bearing for the return estimate)

The conditional next-pin formula is derived in the paper (Prop. prop:first-moment).

lesson.salvage: The first-moment identity is kept and is all the return estimate needs (r is a first moment).

lesson.obstruction: Sanity tests for over-proving: (i) eliminating a cycle produces weight 2 and dividing that bias away to get an unweighted law need not preserve stability, so the argument is genuinely tied to the theta=2 weight; (ii) negative dependence of pin-OUTPUT sets is a different statement from positive equilibrium spin correlations, so no contradiction with ferromagnetism; (iii) a constant function in a reflecting box and mass-reconcentrating transports show that boundary killing and norm loss are essential.
lesson.lesson_statement: The method works because of the weight 2 and of boundary killing; neither can be removed (C13).
lesson.known_in_literature: Consistent with the literature: unweighted interchange negative dependence is BBL/Liggett territory; ferromagnetic positive correlations (Griffiths-type) concern a different object.
lesson.salvage: No content salvaged; the checks support the design.
lesson.what_was_not_learned: The summary does not say whether the model checked d=2 (where Mermin-Wagner forbids order) against the argument; the dimension enters only through d-2-2d nu > alpha and s^{-d/2} (L85, L168), which would fail for d=2.

lesson.obstruction: Could time-dependent forced transports keep returning diffused mass to the source and defeat the leakage estimate? No: permutations preserve l2 norm and cannot restore squared norm already lost to diffusion; a broad harmonic plateau is handled by the same-time flow estimate; because U is not self-adjoint, both the early forward and the late reverse portions are needed.
lesson.lesson_statement: Norm loss is irreversible under permutations; keep both end portions because U is not self-adjoint (C15).
lesson.known_in_literature: Standard (contractivity of doubly substochastic maps).
lesson.salvage: Justifies the two-end design already present at f7.
lesson.what_was_not_learned: None.
